description: Local-first saved-address flow. New src/store/addresses.ts (AsyncStorage, per-user versioned key, pending queue, try/catch, no new dep) + rewire app/checkout.tsx so address GET is instant from local, Save is optimistic (button never network-blocked), and Proceed-to-payment does NO save API call. This is the user's #1 complaint ('save address pe atak raha hai', 'proceed to UPI click nahi kar raha'). Independent of FEAT-002 and FEAT-003.
steps: Create src/store/addresses.ts following src/persistCache.ts conventions EXACTLY: import AsyncStorage from '@react-native-async-storage/async-storage'; import { api } from '../api'; import type { SavedAddress } from '../types'. Keys: const KEY = (userId) => `4astore:addresses:v1:${userId}`; const PENDING_KEY = (userId) => `4astore:addresses:pending:v1:${userId}`. try/catch around EVERY storage and network call.
Implement loadLocal(userId): Promise<SavedAddress[]> — AsyncStorage.getItem(KEY(userId)), JSON.parse, return array; return [] on missing/corrupt/throw.
Implement saveLocal(userId, list): Promise<void> — AsyncStorage.setItem(KEY(userId), JSON.stringify(list)); swallow errors.
Implement upsertLocal(userId, addr): Promise<SavedAddress[]> — loadLocal, replace the entry whose id === addr.id else prepend addr, saveLocal, return the new list.

Implement syncFromServer(userId): Promise<SavedAddress[] | null> — try { const d = await api.get('/addresses'); const list = (d.addresses || []) as SavedAddress[]; await saveLocal(userId, list); return list; } catch { return null; }

Implement queuePending(userId, payload): Promise<void> — read PENDING_KEY array, push payload, write back; swallow errors. Payload shape mirrors checkout.tsx saveAddress(): { action, id, label, receiver_name, phone, house_no, landmark, city, district, state, pincode, latitude, longitude, full_address }. A create payload MUST carry id: undefined (never a temp id).

Implement flushPending(userId): Promise<SavedAddress[] | null> — read the queue; for each payload call api.post('/addresses', payload); on each success reconcile the returned address.id into local storage, replacing any NEGATIVE temp id row that matches (by matching phone+house_no+pincode, or by removing the oldest temp row); on full success clear PENDING_KEY and return the latest local list; on any failure keep the remaining queue and return null. Wrap in try/catch.
Use NEGATIVE temporary ids (-Date.now()) ONLY for optimistic local rows; never send a temp id to the server.

Rewire app/checkout.tsx mount effect (keyed on user?.id): add state const [loadingAddr, setLoadingAddr] = useState(true). On mount: const list = await loadLocal(user.id); setSaved(list); if (list.length) fill(list.find(a=>Number(a.is_default)===1)||list[0]); else setEditorOpen(true); setLoadingAddr(false) — NO network await. Then (not awaited): syncFromServer(user.id).then(srv => { if (srv) merge into setSaved preserving selectedId when that id still exists }); and flushPending(user.id). Remove the old network-on-mount loadAddresses() await.

Rewire saveFromEditor() in app/checkout.tsx: KEEP all existing validation unchanged (name, /^[6-9]\d{9}$/ mobile, address, city, pincode==='824301', verifyVillage + setCity(v.match), buildCustomer with resolveDeliveryCoordinates). Then build an optimistic SavedAddress { id: selectedId ?? -Date.now(), label, receiver_name:c.name, phone:c.mobile, house_no:c.address, landmark:c.landmark, city:c.city, pincode:c.pincode, latitude:c.deliveryLat, longitude:c.deliveryLng, full_address:[c.address,c.city,c.pincode].filter(Boolean).join(', ') }. await upsertLocal(user.id, addr); setSaved(list); setSelectedId(addr.id); setEditorOpen(false); showToast('Address saved / पता सहेजा गया।','success') — synchronously, WITHOUT awaiting the network and WITHOUT holding savingAddr true across the POST. Fire the server write in the background: build the current saveAddress() payload (action: selectedId ? 'update' : 'create', id: selectedId ?? undefined, ...) and api.post('/addresses', payload).then(res => reconcile res.address.id into local+state replacing the temp id).catch(() => queuePending(user.id, payload)).

Remove the blocking save from proceed() in app/checkout.tsx: delete the `try { const s = await saveAddress(c, label); if (s?.id) setSelectedId(s.id); } catch {}` block before setPayOpen(true). Keep ALL validation, age-restricted showConfirm, buildCustomer, setCustomer, setPayOpen(true) unchanged. Proceed must do NO /addresses POST.
Keep the GradientButton Save label/loading tied only to the brief synchronous validation (savingAddr), never to the network POST.
acceptance_criteria: src/store/addresses.ts exists and exports loadLocal, saveLocal, upsertLocal, syncFromServer, queuePending, flushPending with the signatures above and no new npm dependency.
app/checkout.tsx reads addresses from local storage on mount with no network await; a returning user sees their saved address immediately (no spinner unless local is empty on first-ever use).
Saving an address closes the editor and shows the success toast immediately; the Save button is not disabled/spinning waiting on the network.
proceed() contains no /addresses POST; tapping Proceed opens the payment sheet without a save round-trip.
Running `npm run typecheck` yields no new TypeScript errors beyond the known app.config.ts usesCleartextTraffic error.
verification: From c:\xampp\htdocs\static4a\.worktrees\app-local-first\4astore-v2\mobile run `npm install` (once) then `npm run typecheck`; confirm the only error is the pre-existing app.config.ts usesCleartextTraffic one.
Read-through: confirm checkout mount uses loadLocal before any network, saveFromEditor does not await the POST, and proceed() has no api.post('/addresses', ...).
findings: DONE. New file src/store/addresses.ts (no new deps; AsyncStorage + api only). Export surface: loadLocal(userId): Promise<SavedAddress[]>, saveLocal(userId, list): Promise<void>, upsertLocal(userId, addr): Promise<SavedAddress[]>, syncFromServer(userId): Promise<SavedAddress[]|null>, queuePending(userId, payload): Promise<void>, flushPending(userId): Promise<SavedAddress[]|null>, plus an exported interface PendingPayload { action:'create'|'update'; id?:number; label; receiver_name; phone; house_no; landmark?; city; district?; state?; pincode; latitude?; longitude?; full_address? }. Keys: 4astore:addresses:v1:<userId> and 4astore:addresses:pending:v1:<userId>. userId param is typed number|string. Temp ids are NEGATIVE (-Date.now()); create payloads send id: undefined. Reconciliation in flushPending (and checkout's inline save): match a negative temp row by phone+house_no+pincode, else fall back to the OLDEST temp row (oldest = largest/least-negative id, since -Date.now() grows more negative over time); replace it with the server address.id. flushPending stops at first POST failure, persists the remaining queue, returns null; clears PENDING_KEY and returns loadLocal() on full success. checkout.tsx rewired: added state loadingAddr (default true), gated the Proceed GradientButton with disabled={loadingAddr}. Mount effect (keyed on user?.id) now does loadLocal first (no network await) then fires syncFromServer + flushPending in the background, with a cancelled guard; captures const userId once to keep strict-null narrowing across awaits. Old network loadAddresses() helper and the standalone saveAddress() helper were REMOVED (saveAddress became dead code once proceed() stopped calling it). saveFromEditor() keeps all validation unchanged, writes the optimistic row via upsertLocal, closes editor + success toast synchronously, then fires api.post('/addresses', payload) in the background: on success reconciles the real id into local+state, on failure calls queuePending(userId, payload). savingAddr is only held across the synchronous local write, never across the POST. proceed() no longer calls api.post('/addresses') at all — it builds the customer and opens the payment sheet directly. The address POST payload still carries district:'Aurangabad', state:'Bihar' (unchanged from the prior saveAddress helper) so the server shape is untouched. Verification: npm install ran once; npm run typecheck exits with exactly ONE error = the known app.config.ts usesCleartextTraffic one (app.config.ts:39). No tracking/rider/server files touched; no new npm dependency; no visual restyle beyond adding disabled on an existing button. For later steps: reuse these store functions (loadLocal/saveLocal/upsertLocal/syncFromServer/queuePending/flushPending) rather than re-GETting; the pending-queue + negative-temp-id pattern here is the template for any other optimistic local-first write.
